name: C2 — Mastery
description: Read novels, parse classical-flavored prose, debate philosophy, and switch register at will.

topics.title: Classical echoes (文言)
topics.description: The 之/其/所/而 family — and how they survive in modern formal writing

guide.intro: You will not be writing 文言 (wényán, classical Chinese) — almost no one does. But every Chinese newspaper editorial, legal document, government report, and serious novel is studded with classical particles, fossilized syntax, and four-character compressions that only make sense if you can read the classical underneath. Treat this as the X-ray vision unit.

sections.text: 之 (zhī) — the all-purpose connector

In modern colloquial Chinese 之 is replaced by 的. In formal writing 之 returns: it links a modifier to a noun (愛國之心 — "a heart of patriotism"), substitutes for an object pronoun (取而代之 — "take it and replace it"), and lurks inside dozens of 成語. Whenever you see 之 in a modern text, mentally swap in 的 or "it" and the sentence usually clicks.

rows.translation: What is said has reason — "that has merit."
To sum it up — used to open a closing paragraph.
A treasure of no price — priceless.

sections.text: 其 (qí) — "its / their / the said"

其 is the formal third-person possessive and a gentle determiner. In a contract you will read 其責任 (its/the responsibility). In an editorial: 其原因有三 (the reasons are three). Notice it never takes 的 after it.

rows.translation: In fact (lit. "its truth").
Each gets their proper place.
Among them / within it.

sections.text: 所 (suǒ) — turns a verb into "that which is V-ed"

所 + verb makes a passive-flavored relative clause: 所說 (that which is said), 所做 (that which is done), 所謂 (so-called). Pair it with 的 in modern usage to keep it readable: 我所說的話 — "the words I said." Reporters love this construction.

rows.translation: As is known to all — newspaper opener.
Unprecedented (lit. "never before existed").
The so-called experts — heavy with skepticism.

sections.text: 而 (ér) — "and / yet / and so"

而 fuses two predicates. Coordinative (年輕而有為 — young and capable), adversative (富而不驕 — rich yet not arrogant), or sequential (起而行之 — rise and act). Modern formal speech is full of it: spoken 而 sounds bookish; written 而 sounds polished.

Quick test: if you can replace 而 with English "and", "yet", or "thus" without losing the sense, you've parsed it. If none fit, you're probably looking at the fossilized 然而 (however) or 因而 (therefore).
Other classical fossils still alive

rows: 以…为… ("take X as Y"), 以便, 以免
若…则… ("if…then…"), 否则, 然则
几乎, 在乎, 不亦乐乎
记者, 学者, 读者, 强者
之乎者也 — the cliché of pedantry

sections.text: 之乎者也 (zhī hū zhě yě) is itself an idiom — it means "empty pedantic talk," mocking someone who hides behind classical jargon.

Don't conflate the two 也. Modern 也 is the high-frequency adverb "also / too" (我也去 — "I'm going too"). Classical 也 is a sentence-final marker that functioned roughly as a copula or assertion (… ， … 也 — "… is the case"). Same character, completely different jobs. In the table above, 也 is listed under its classical job; in everyday reading 99% of 也 you'll see is the modern adverb.
Literary number pairs

In literary or written-elevated register, paired numbers function adverbially to mean "a few / scattered." 一二 (yī èr) — "one or two," 三五 (sān wǔ) — "a handful," 七八 (qī bā) — "seven or eight, a small group." These appear in essays, captions, and novels — almost never in speech.

rows.source: 三五 好友 圍爐 夜話。
rows.translation: A handful of close friends chatting around the stove at night.

rows.source: 一二 行人 匆匆 而 過。
rows.pinyin: Yī èr xíngrén cōngcōng ér guò.
rows.translation: A pedestrian or two hurrying past.

lessons.title: 之 in modern prose
lessons.description: Spot 之 inside fixed phrases and editorials

exercises.prompt: In a modern editorial, 之 most often functions like which colloquial particle?
exercises.answer: 的
exercises.explanation: 之 is the formal counterpart of 的 — it links a modifier to a noun in elevated register. The other particles (地 adverbial, 得 complement, 而 connector) handle distinct grammatical jobs.

exercises.prompt: the 之-idiom to its meaning
An economics column ends with "總而言之，通脹壓力未減。" What is the writer signaling?
exercises.answer: A summarizing conclusion
exercises.explanation: 總而言之 = "in conclusion / all in all" — a discourse marker for the wrap-up paragraph.

exercises.prompt: "愛國之心" (ài guó zhī xīn) translates as ___
exercises.answer: A heart of patriotism

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 之 in its classical-modern formal sense (modifier-linker)?
options: 他 走 之 後 我 才 來
國家 之 強盛 在 於 民
我 也 去 之
之 是 什麼 意思
exercises.answer: 國家 之 強盛 在 於 民
exercises.explanation: 國家之強盛 ("the strength of the nation") uses 之 as the formal modifier-linker = 的. The other options misuse 之 — option 1 is a fixed adverbial (走之後 is colloquial 之後), the others ungrammatical.

exercises.prompt: Build a long formal sentence: "The development of artificial intelligence is the great trend of our age, and it is irreversible."
exercises.answer: 人工智慧 之 發展 乃 時代 之 大勢 不可 逆轉

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads a formal editorial line. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 言之有理，行之有效，方為治世之策
options: 言之有理，行之有效，方為治世之策
說得有道理，做得很有效，才是治理的好辦法
言而有信，行而果斷，是治世的關鍵
話說得對，事做得好，國家就能治理
exercises.answer: 言之有理，行之有效，方為治世之策
exercises.explanation: Three uses of 之 (modifier-linker) plus 方為 (literary 才是) and 之策 (formal -strategy). The other options paraphrase the same idea in modern colloquial or near-colloquial register.

exercises.prompt: each 之-construction to the modern 的-equivalent (or paraphrase)

pairs.right: 改革的困難 — the difficulty of reform
一天的功夫 — a single day's effort
國家的根本 — the root of the nation
切身的痛苦 — pain felt in the flesh

exercises.prompt: An editorial reads "非一日之功可解." The 非…可… pattern is:
options: Classical negation pattern — "not something a day's effort can solve"
exercises.answer: Classical negation pattern — "not something a day's effort can solve"
exercises.explanation: 非 X 可 Y = literary "not X-able by Y" — a fossilized classical negation that survives in editorials. Modern colloquial would say "不是一天就能解決的."

exercises.prompt: An editorial closes: "扶貧攻堅，非 ___ 之 ___ 可 成." Fill the two-character pair (a single day's effort).
exercises.answer: 一日 之 功
exercises.explanation: 非一日之功可成 — "cannot be done in a day's effort." A boilerplate editorial closer that quietly hedges expectations.

lessons.title: 其 and 所 — formal relatives
lessons.description: The two particles that turn modern prose into a contract

exercises.prompt: "其原因有三" most naturally means:
exercises.answer: The reasons are three
exercises.explanation: 其 = "its/their"; 有三 = "are three (in number)." Classic essay-opener.

exercises.prompt: "所謂的專家" carries which tone?
exercises.answer: Skeptical / dismissive
exercises.explanation: 所謂 = "so-called." Almost always loaded with doubt or sarcasm in modern usage.

exercises.prompt: the 所-phrase to its meaning

pairs.right: Naturally / as a matter of course

exercises.prompt: Build: "This is what we said." (formal)
exercises.answer: 這 是 我們 所 說 的

exercises.prompt: A contract reads "其責任 由 甲方 承擔." 其 here refers to:
options: The responsibility just defined in the prior clause
exercises.answer: The responsibility just defined in the prior clause
exercises.explanation: 其 = formal possessive/anaphor — "its responsibility" (i.e., the responsibility belonging to whatever was last named). Standard contract glue.

exercises.prompt: Build a contract clause: "The responsibility for it shall be borne by Party A; the costs shall also be paid by Party A."
exercises.answer: 其 責任 由 甲方 承擔 其 費用 亦 由 甲方 支付

exercises.prompt: A reporter reads a sentence stuffed with 所 and 其. Pick the formal version.
exercises.spokenText: 眾所周知，其影響之深遠，前所未有
options: 眾所周知，其影響之深遠，前所未有
大家都知道，這影響很深遠，從來沒有過
據說，這事影響很大，是頭一回
我們清楚，影響很大，史上第一次
exercises.answer: 眾所周知，其影響之深遠，前所未有
exercises.explanation: Two 所-constructions (眾所周知, 前所未有), 其 + 之 chain. The distractors paraphrase in modern colloquial, official, or semi-formal registers.

exercises.prompt: A government white paper writes "___ 周知，氣候變化已成全球共同挑戰." Fill in the four-character all-knowing opener.
exercises.answer: 眾所
exercises.explanation: 眾所周知 = "as is known to all" — the canonical 所-construction opener for editorials and policy papers.

exercises.prompt: each 其/所 phrase to its discourse function
Which sentence uses 所 INCORRECTLY for a C2 reader?
exercises.answer: 我所吃飯
exercises.explanation: 所 + verb forms a noun-clause but only with transitive verbs taking an object that becomes the head — and 所吃飯 is ungrammatical because 吃飯 is already V+O. Correct would be 我所吃的飯. The other three are well-formed.

lessons.title: 而 — the bookish glue
lessons.description: And, yet, thus — depending on what flanks it

exercises.prompt: "富而不驕" (fù ér bù jiāo) means:
exercises.answer: Rich, yet not arrogant
exercises.explanation: Adversative 而 — "X yet not Y." A standard literary praise pattern.

exercises.prompt: Pick the most natural translation: "年輕而有為"
exercises.answer: Young and accomplished
exercises.explanation: Coordinative 而 — both qualities hold. 有為 (yǒu wéi) = "capable / promising."

exercises.prompt: Build: "He spoke briefly yet to the point."
exercises.answer: 他 說 得 簡短 而 中肯

exercises.prompt: Modern formal connector "然而" means ___
exercises.answer: However
exercises.explanation: 然而 = literally "yet-and"; the workhorse contrastive in essays.

exercises.prompt: A literary-register sentence is read aloud. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 眾所周知，前所未有之變局，非一日之功可解
options: 眾所周知，前所未有之變局，非一日之功可解
大家都知道，這種沒見過的局面，不是一天就能解決的
我們都明白，這是從來沒有過的事情，需要時間
據報道，目前局勢複雜，有關部門正在研究
exercises.answer: 眾所周知，前所未有之變局，非一日之功可解
exercises.explanation: Classical fossils all stacked: 眾所周知 (所), 前所未有 (所), 之 (formal of), 非…可解 (classical negation pattern). The other options say similar things in modern colloquial or official register.

exercises.prompt: "取而代之" — what is the role of 而 here?
exercises.answer: Sequential — "and then" (take and replace)
exercises.explanation: 取而代之 = "take, and replace it." The 而 here is the sequential connector — first 取, then 代之.

exercises.prompt: Build a literary-balanced sentence: "He is young yet steady; he speaks little but acts decisively."
exercises.answer: 他 年輕 而 沉穩 言 寡 而 行 果

exercises.prompt: the 而-phrase to its function (coordinative / adversative / sequential)

pairs.right: Fossilized discourse marker — to sum up

exercises.prompt: An essay reads: "政策推行 三年，___ 收效甚微." Fill the formal contrastive connector (one character).
exercises.answer: 然
exercises.explanation: 然 (or 然而) — formal "yet/however." The single-character 然 is the most literary; 然而 is essay-standard. 但 is more conversational.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence-final 也 is the CLASSICAL copula (not the modern "also")?
options: 他 也 不 知道
此 乃 國 之 大 事 也
你 也 來 了
exercises.answer: 此 乃 國 之 大 事 也
exercises.explanation: Classical 也 is sentence-final and assertion-like (≈ "is the case"). Pairs naturally with 此乃 ("this is") + 之 in literary register. The other three are modern adverbial 也 = "also/too."

lessons.title: 以、則、者 — the rest of the toolkit
lessons.description: Three more classical particles you'll trip over weekly

exercises.prompt: "以…為…" means:
options: Take X as / regard X as Y
exercises.answer: Take X as / regard X as Y
exercises.explanation: 以學生為本 = "take students as the foundation" — boilerplate education-policy phrasing. (The canonical example is 以人為本 — rén-běn — "put people first," the Hu-era policy slogan.)

exercises.prompt: Build: "Our company puts the customer first." (use 以…為…)
exercises.answer: 我們 公司 以 客戶 為 本

exercises.prompt: "若…則…" is the formal counterpart of which everyday pattern?
exercises.answer: 要是…就…
exercises.explanation: Both are conditionals. 若…則… is the literary register; 要是…就… is colloquial.

exercises.prompt: the 者-noun to its meaning
"之乎者也" describes someone who ___
exercises.answer: Speaks pretentiously / hides behind pedantic jargon
exercises.explanation: All four are classical particles bundled together — a label for hollow learnedness.

exercises.prompt: the classical compression to its modern function (these still appear in editorials and legal documents)

pairs.right: Therefore / for this reason (= 因此, formal)
That being so / in that case (= 那麼)
Why is that? (rhetorical question, = 為什麼)
X's relation to Y / X compared to Y

exercises.prompt: A legal opinion contains: "是以本院駁回原告之訴訟請求." The 是以 functions as:
exercises.answer: A formal "therefore"
exercises.explanation: 是以 = 因此 / 所以 in elevated register. Watch for it in court opinions, government white papers, and editorial conclusions.

exercises.prompt: Build a formal conditional: "If the policy goes through, then the people will benefit; if not, then losses will mount day by day."
exercises.answer: 政策 若 行 則 民 受 其 利 不 行 則 損 日 增

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads a 文言-flavored editorial close. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 是以本部門決定，自即日起，相關政策依法施行
options: 是以本部門決定，自即日起，相關政策依法施行
因此我們部門決定，從今天開始，相關政策按法律執行
所以這個部門決定，從這天開始，要按規定辦理
據此，部門已經決定，今天起就開始執行
exercises.answer: 是以本部門決定，自即日起，相關政策依法施行
exercises.explanation: 是以 (formal 因此), 本部門 (this department), 自即日起 (formal 從今天開始), 依法施行 (formal "executed in accordance with law") — four register markers. The distractors translate the same content into ordinary or near-formal Chinese.

exercises.prompt: Pair completion: "___ 你 已 決定，則 不必 再 猶豫." Fill the literary premise marker (two characters).
exercises.answer: 既然
exercises.explanation: 既然…則… (literary) = 既然…就… (modern). Both halves carry the conclusion forward; 則 is the bookish counterpart of 就.

exercises.prompt: Which use of 以 is the CLASSICAL "in order to / so as to" (purpose)?
options: 他 以 學生 的 身份 發言
我 以 此 為 戒 以 免 重 蹈 覆轍
用 這個 方法 解決
我 以為 他 不來
exercises.answer: 我 以 此 為 戒 以 免 重 蹈 覆轍
exercises.explanation: The second 以 in 以免 ("so as to avoid") is the classical purpose marker — same root as 以便 ("so as to facilitate"). The first 以 here is 以…為… ("take… as…"); option 1 is identity-marking 以; option 4 is the verb 以為 ("think").

lessons.title: Dialogue: Book club on a classical text
lessons.description: Debate a passage from 莊子 and how its particles survive in modern prose.

exercises.prompt: Book club on a classical text

turns.speaker: wei
turns.text: 今晚我們讀《莊子》的一段，關於無用之用。(jīn wǎn wǒmen dú zhuāngzǐ de yī duàn, guānyú wú yòng zhī yòng.)
turns.spokenText: 今晚我們讀《莊子》的一段，關於無用之用。

turns.speaker: wei
turns.text: 原文是「人皆知有用之用，而莫知無用之用也」。(rén jiē zhī yǒu yòng zhī yòng, ér mò zhī wú yòng zhī yòng yě.)
turns.spokenText: 人皆知有用之用，而莫知無用之用也。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Which colloquial particle does 之 here correspond to?

turns.speaker: wei
turns.text: 對，「有用之用」即「有用的用處」。那句末的「也」呢？(duì, yǒu yòng zhī yòng jí yǒu yòng de yòng chu. nà jù mò de yě ne?)
turns.spokenText: 對，「有用之用」即「有用的用處」。那句末的「也」呢？

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: What is sentence-final 也 doing here?
options: Classical assertion marker, roughly a copula (yě – classical)
turns.answer: Classical assertion marker, roughly a copula (yě – classical)

turns.speaker: wei
turns.text: 正是。現代社論裡也常用「不可不察也」收尾。(zhèng shì. xiàn dài shè lùn lǐ yě cháng yòng bù kě bù chá yě shōu wěi.)
turns.spokenText: 正是。現代社論裡也常用「不可不察也」收尾。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Fill the classical particle: "as for ..." (其...) — give the formal third-person/topic marker.
turns.after: 言深遠，發人深省。(yán shēn yuǎn, fā rén shēn xǐng.)

turns.speaker: wei
turns.text: 妙！「其言」即「他的話」。最後看「眾所周知」之「所」。(miào! qí yán jí tā de huà. zuì hòu kàn zhòng suǒ zhōu zhī zhī suǒ.)
turns.spokenText: 妙！「其言」即「他的話」。最後看「眾所周知」之「所」。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 所 + verb forms what kind of phrase?
options: A passive-flavored relative clause: "that which is V-ed"
turns.answer: A passive-flavored relative clause: "that which is V-ed"

turns.speaker: wei
turns.text: 好。下週讀《論語》，請把今晚的之乎者也都消化掉。(hǎo. xià zhōu dú lúnyǔ, qǐng bǎ jīn wǎn de zhī hū zhě yě dōu xiāo huà diào.)
turns.spokenText: 好。下週讀《論語》，請把今晚的之乎者也都消化掉。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Complete the closing idiom — "unprecedented": 前___未有.

turns.speaker: wei
turns.text: 前所未有的進步。下次見！(qián suǒ wèi yǒu de jìn bù. xià cì jiàn!)
turns.spokenText: 前所未有的進步。下次見！

topics.title: Tang poetry foundations
topics.description: 李白, 杜甫, 王維 — the lines every educated speaker can quote

guide.intro: Tang dynasty (618–907) poetry is the cultural reservoir Chinese speakers draw on the way English speakers reach for Shakespeare. You don't need to read every poem — but the half-dozen lines below are quoted in WeChat moments, business toasts, news headlines, and movie titles. Knowing them is the difference between hearing a language and hearing a culture.

sections.text: 李白 — the romantic

Lǐ Bái (701–762), nicknamed 詩仙 (the Poetry Immortal). Famous for moonlit drinking, untethered imagination, and homesickness. His 靜夜思 (Quiet Night Thoughts) is the first poem Chinese children memorize.

rows.translation: Before my bed, bright moonlight —
I wondered if it were frost on the ground.
Lifting my head, I gazed at the bright moon —
Lowering it, I thought of my hometown.

sections.text: 故鄉 (gù xiāng — hometown) is the most-loaded word in classical Chinese. It still freights modern songs, Lunar New Year speeches, and diaspora literature.

Textual note: the 床前明月光 wording above is the Ming-dynasty redaction (the version every Chinese child memorizes today). The earlier Tang variant reads 床前看月光 / 疑是地上霜 / 舉頭望山月 / 低頭思故鄉. If you ever see 看月光 / 望山月 in an academic citation, it isn't a typo — it's the older edition.
杜甫 — the conscience

Dù Fǔ (712–770), 詩聖 (the Poetry Sage). Where Lǐ Bái soars, Dù Fǔ documents — war, hunger, the displaced family. His phrase 國破山河在 ("the nation shattered, mountains and rivers remain") is quoted whenever a country loses something it cannot replace.

rows.translation: The state is broken; the mountains and rivers remain.
Spring in the city — grass and trees grow thick.
Moved by the times, even flowers shed tears.

sections.text: 王維 — the painter-monk

Wáng Wéi (701–761) painted in words and wrote on silk. His couplets are nearly silent: a stream, a bell, a single bird. The phrase 詩中有畫，畫中有詩 ("poetry in his paintings, paintings in his poetry") was coined to describe him.

rows.translation: Empty mountain — no one in sight.
Only the echo of voices is heard.
Bright moon shines between the pines.

sections.text: 蘇軾 — the Song-dynasty bonus

Sū Shì (1037–1101) is technically Song, not Tang, but you cannot graduate without him. His line 但願人長久，千里共嬋娟 ("may we live long and share the moon's beauty across a thousand li") is the standard Mid-Autumn Festival blessing — printed on mooncake boxes nationwide.

rows.translation: May people endure (live long).
And share, across a thousand li, the moon's beauty.

rows.pinyin: Bù shí Lú shān zhēn miàn mù
rows.translation: I cannot see Mount Lu's true face —

rows.pinyin: Zhǐ yuán shēn zài cǐ shān zhōng
rows.translation: Only because I myself am in the mountain.

sections.text: Su Shi's couplet shares a sensibility with the proverb 當局者迷 ("the one inside the game is confused") — but the proverb itself comes from 舊唐書 (the Old Book of Tang), not from 題西林壁. They are quoted side by side because they say the same thing from different angles.

lessons.title: 李白 — moon and home
lessons.description: The 靜夜思 quartet

exercises.prompt: 李白 is known by which honorific?
exercises.answer: 詩仙 — Poetry Immortal

exercises.prompt: Reassemble: "Lifting my head, I gazed at the bright moon."
exercises.answer: 舉 頭 望 明 月

exercises.prompt: In 靜夜思, what does the poet think the moonlight resembles on the floor? (Answer in English.)
exercises.answer: Frost
exercises.explanation: 疑是地上霜 — "I wondered if it were frost on the ground." The sleepless homesick image.

exercises.prompt: the line to its theme
A diaspora speaker tells the audience "低頭思故鄉" — they are signaling:
options: Homesickness, by quoting the most-recognized line in Chinese poetry
A literal description of their posture
exercises.answer: Homesickness, by quoting the most-recognized line in Chinese poetry
exercises.explanation: Quoting 低頭思故鄉 is the cultural shorthand for missing home — every Chinese speaker recognizes 靜夜思 from childhood.

exercises.prompt: Reassemble the full quartet of 靜夜思 in correct order.
exercises.answer: 床前 明月 光 疑是 地上 霜 舉頭 望 明月 低頭 思 故鄉

exercises.prompt: A speaker recites a line in classical-recital cadence (slow, drawn syllables). Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 舉頭望明月，低頭思故鄉
options: 舉頭望明月，低頭思故鄉
床前明月光，疑是地上霜
空山不見人，但聞人語響

topics.title: Rhetoric and argumentation
topics.description: Parallel structures, hedges, and the rhythm of formal Chinese

guide.intro: Mandarin formal writing has a rhythm. It loves parallel pairs, four-character cadences, and concessive hedges that English would handle with one comma. Internalizing these patterns is what separates the C1 essay ("correct") from the C2 essay ("this could be in 人民日报").

sections.text: Parallel pair: 一方面…另一方面…
"On one hand…on the other…" The skeleton of every balanced opinion piece. The two clauses should be the same length and grammatical shape — that's where Chinese rhetoric earns its style points.

rows.source: 一方面 我們要發展經濟，另一方面 也要保護環境。
rows.pinyin: Yì fāngmiàn wǒmen yào fāzhǎn jīngjì, lìng yì fāngmiàn yě yào bǎohù huánjìng.
rows.translation: On one hand we must grow the economy; on the other, we must also protect the environment.

sections.text: Concessive: …也好，…也罷
"Whether X or Y — either way…" A literary, faintly resigned tone. You'll see it in op-eds and novelistic narration. The pair must mirror — same word class, similar length.

rows.source: 成功 也好，失敗 也罷，過程 才 重要。
rows.pinyin: Chénggōng yě hǎo, shībài yě bà, guòchéng cái zhòngyào.
rows.translation: Success or failure — what matters is the process.

rows.source: 你 信 也好，不信 也罷，事實 就 在 那裡。
rows.pinyin: Nǐ xìn yě hǎo, bú xìn yě bà, shìshí jiù zài nàlǐ.
rows.translation: Believe it or not, the facts are right there.

sections.text: Choice and preference: 與其…不如… / 寧可…也不…
Two paired patterns for ranking options. 與其 X 不如 Y — "rather than X, better Y." 寧可 X 也不 Y — "would rather X than Y." Both are written-register; both make the speaker sound deliberative.

rows.source: 與其 抱怨，不如 行動。
rows.translation: Rather than complain, take action.

rows.source: 他 寧可 辭職，也不 妥協。
rows.pinyin: Tā nìngkě cízhí, yě bù tuǒxié.
rows.translation: He would rather quit than compromise.

sections.text: Discourse shift: 倒是
倒是 (dào shì) — "on the contrary / actually / as it happens." A discourse marker that signals a gentle reversal of expectation. Not the dramatic 反而 — softer, more conversational-formal.

rows.source: 他 平時 話 不多，關鍵 時刻 倒是 很 果斷。
rows.pinyin: Tā píngshí huà bù duō, guānjiàn shíkè dàoshì hěn guǒduàn.
rows.translation: He's usually quiet, but at critical moments he's actually very decisive.

rows.source: 你 這麼 一 說，我 倒是 想起來 了。
rows.pinyin: Nǐ zhème yì shuō, wǒ dàoshì xiǎng qǐlái le.
rows.translation: Now that you mention it, I do remember.

sections.text: Building from a premise: 既然…就…
"Given that X, then Y." The premise is treated as agreed-upon — it shifts the conversation forward. Distinct from 因為…所以… (causal) and 如果…就… (hypothetical).

rows.source: 既然 你 已經 決定 了，就 別 再 猶豫。
rows.pinyin: Jìrán nǐ yǐjīng juédìng le, jiù bié zài yóuyù.
rows.translation: Since you've already decided, stop hesitating.

sections.text: Cause-and-effect chain: 之所以…是因為…
"The reason X is because Y." Stylistically inverted from English — Chinese leads with the consequence and only later names the cause. Beloved by editorialists building suspense.

rows.source: 他 之所以 成功，是 因為 他 從 不 放棄。
rows.pinyin: Tā zhī suǒyǐ chénggōng, shì yīnwèi tā cóng bù fàngqì.
rows.translation: The reason he succeeded is that he never gives up.

sections.text: Four-character rhythm rule: when in doubt, balance. 不僅…而且… is fine; 不僅 simple, 而且 ornate sounds wrong. Match the weight of the two clauses and your sentence will sound native.

一方面經濟，另一方面環境
一方面要發展，另一方面我們必須立即推進環境保護工作
exercises.answer: 一方面要發展經濟，另一方面要保護環境
exercises.explanation: Both clauses: 要 + 2-char verb + 2-char object. Same syllable count, same shape. The padded options break the rhythm.

exercises.prompt: Build a long balanced parallel: "On one hand we must heed people's hopes; on the other we must respond to people's worries."
exercises.answer: 一方面 我們 要 傾聽 民意 另一方面 我們 要 回應 民憂

exercises.prompt: the parallel pattern to its essay function

pairs.right: Not only X but also Y — escalation
Either X or Y — listing alternatives

exercises.prompt: Which sentence shows the strongest 4-character cadence balance?
options: 我們要重視效率，同時也要顧及到公平問題
效率是重要的，公平也是重要的
我們應當兼顧效率和公平這兩個方面
exercises.answer: 效率優先，公平為本
exercises.explanation: Two 4-character clauses with parallel grammar (noun + verb + noun's role). Editorial cadence at its tightest. The other options say the same thing but lose the rhythm.

exercises.prompt: Complete the balanced pair: "成功 ___ 失敗 ___ 過程 才 重要." (Fill the two concessive markers.)
exercises.answer: 也好 也罷
exercises.explanation: 也好…也罷 — "whether X or Y, either way…" Literary concessive pair. Both halves must be matched in length.

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads a long compound sentence. Pick the version with the most balanced parallel rhythm.
exercises.spokenText: 教育之於個人，關乎前途；教育之於國家，關乎未來
options: 教育之於個人，關乎前途；教育之於國家，關乎未來
教育對個人來說是關於前途的事情；教育對國家來說則關乎未來
教育對個人有影響；教育對國家也很重要
教育之於個人關乎前途，對國家來說關乎未來這一重要議題
exercises.answer: 教育之於個人，關乎前途；教育之於國家，關乎未來
exercises.explanation: Two clauses, perfectly mirrored: 教育 之於 X，關乎 Y. Same length, same shape, classical 之於 as the connector. The distractors all break the symmetry.

exercises.prompt: Why does Chinese formal writing chase clause-length balance more aggressively than English?
options: Chinese has no other rhythm — it's impossible to write without it
Cultural-rhetorical convention rooted in classical 駢文 (parallel prose) — balanced rhythm signals seriousness and care
Editors enforce it via word counts
exercises.answer: Cultural-rhetorical convention rooted in classical 駢文 (parallel prose) — balanced rhythm signals seriousness and care
exercises.explanation: 駢文 (parallel prose) trained centuries of writers to value matched clauses. Modern editorial Chinese inherits the instinct: balanced rhythm = serious writer. Imbalanced clauses sound rushed even when grammatically fine.

lessons.title: 也好 / 也罷 — concessive shrug
lessons.description: Either way, the point stands

exercises.prompt: "成功也好，失敗也罷，過程才重要" is closest to:
options: Success matters more than the process
Win or lose, what matters is the journey
Failure is the mother of success
Don't try and you can't fail
exercises.answer: Win or lose, what matters is the journey

exercises.prompt: Build: "Believe it or not, the facts are right there."
exercises.answer: 你 信 也好 不信 也罷 事實 就 在 那裡

exercises.prompt: What register does …也好，…也罷 belong to?
exercises.answer: Literary / op-ed register
exercises.explanation: It carries a slightly resigned, philosophical tone. You hear it in newspaper columns and literary fiction, rarely in casual chat.

exercises.prompt: the C2-register connector pattern to what it does

pairs.right: Whether X or Y, either way…
The reason X is that Y

exercises.prompt: Build a long concessive sentence: "Whether the policy is finally adopted or rejected, public discussion has already gone deep."
exercises.answer: 政策 通過 也好 否決 也罷 公共 討論 已 走 向 深入

exercises.prompt: A columnist reads a literary concessive line. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 成功也好，失敗也罷，過程才是真正的財富
options: 成功也好，失敗也罷，過程才是真正的財富
成功或者失敗都沒關係，過程才重要
不管是成功還是失敗，過程是關鍵
無論成功失敗，過程是真財富
exercises.answer: 成功也好，失敗也罷，過程才是真正的財富
exercises.explanation: 也好…也罷 + 才是 + multi-character noun phrase carries the literary register. The distractors paraphrase the same idea in everyday or semi-formal Chinese.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence misuses 也好…也罷?
options: 信也好，不信也罷，事實就在那裡
成功也好，失敗也罷，過程最重要
他來也好，沒來也罷，會議照常
天氣也好，所以我去散步
exercises.answer: 天氣也好，所以我去散步
exercises.explanation: Here 也好 means "is fine" (modern adjective use), not the concessive pair. The pattern 也好…也罷 requires two contrasting alternatives — option 4 has only one and is using 也好 in a totally different sense.

exercises.prompt: An op-ed reads: "贊 ___ ，罵 ___ ，時間 終 會 給出 答案." Fill the two concessive markers.
exercises.answer: 也好 也罷
exercises.explanation: 贊也好，罵也罷 — "praise or scold, either way…" Two 1-character verbs balanced perfectly under the concessive frame.

exercises.prompt: the concessive pattern to its register subtlety

pairs.right: Highly classical — "even if X, still Y"

exercises.prompt: A novelist writes: "贏也好，輸也罷，他都已經走得太遠." The 也好…也罷 here contributes:
options: A weary, fatalistic tone — outcome no longer matters
exercises.answer: A weary, fatalistic tone — outcome no longer matters
exercises.explanation: 也好…也罷 carries a faintly resigned quality that's perfect for a novelist signaling that a character has passed the point of caring about outcomes. That tonal coloring is what separates it from the neutral 無論…還是….

lessons.title: 之所以…是因為…
lessons.description: Lead with the consequence, end with the cause

exercises.prompt: Build: "The reason he succeeded is that he never gives up."
exercises.answer: 他 之所以 成功 是因為 他 從不 放棄

exercises.prompt: Why might a writer prefer 之所以…是因為… over 因為…所以…?
options: It foregrounds the result and makes the cause feel like a reveal
It is grammatically required after 但是
exercises.answer: It foregrounds the result and makes the cause feel like a reveal
exercises.explanation: Inverting the order is a rhetorical move — it lets the writer build small suspense before naming the cause.

exercises.prompt: "既然你已經決定了，___ 別再猶豫。" — fill the blank.
exercises.answer: 就
exercises.explanation: 既然…就… is the fixed pair. Both halves carry the conclusion forward.

exercises.prompt: Build a long causal-reveal sentence: "The reason this reform has succeeded is precisely that it places the people's livelihood first."
exercises.answer: 這 項 改革 之所以 成功 正是 因為 它 把 民生 放在 首位

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads an inverted causal sentence. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 他之所以堅持下來，是因為他從未忘記最初的承諾
options: 他之所以堅持下來，是因為他從未忘記最初的承諾
他堅持下來是因為他沒忘記最初的承諾
因為他沒忘記承諾，所以他堅持下來了
他從未忘記承諾，所以他堅持下來
exercises.answer: 他之所以堅持下來，是因為他從未忘記最初的承諾
exercises.explanation: 之所以…是因為… is the essay-style inversion (lead with consequence, reveal the cause). The other three express the same idea in 因為…所以… or modern colloquial frames.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 之所以 INCORRECTLY?
options: 他之所以成功，是因為堅持
她之所以離開，是因為身體原因
我之所以喜歡，是因為它很美
之所以下雨，今天不出門
exercises.answer: 之所以下雨，今天不出門
exercises.explanation: 之所以 must attach to a clause as the consequence ("the reason X is…"), and is then completed by 是因為 + cause. Option 4 misuses it as a stand-in for 因為. The other three are well-formed 之所以…是因為… inversions.

exercises.prompt: Complete the inversion: "中國 經濟 之所以 能夠 持續 增長，___ 改革開放 政策 的 推動." Fill the cause-marker (3 characters).
exercises.answer: 是因為
exercises.explanation: 之所以…是因為… is the fixed inverted pair. The cause clause (改革開放政策的推動) follows 是因為 as the rhetorical reveal.

exercises.prompt: the causal connector to its register
A columnist writes: "這家公司之所以失去市場，是因為它忘記了使用者." The rhetorical effect of leading with 之所以 is:
options: It builds suspense — the failure is named first; the cause becomes the reveal
exercises.answer: It builds suspense — the failure is named first; the cause becomes the reveal
exercises.explanation: 因為…所以… presents cause then effect; 之所以…是因為… inverts to lead with effect. The inversion turns the cause into a punchline — exactly what columnists want for impact.

exercises.prompt: Build a premise sentence (既然…就…): "Since the people have given their trust, then we must repay them with effort."
exercises.answer: 既然 人民 給予 我們 信任 我們 就 應當 以 努力 回報

lessons.title: Choice, preference, and 倒是
lessons.description: 與其…不如, 寧可…也不, and the discourse marker 倒是

exercises.prompt: "與其抱怨，不如行動." The structure 與其…不如… expresses:
options: A preference: rather than X, better Y
exercises.answer: A preference: rather than X, better Y
exercises.explanation: 與其 (yǔqí) sets up the dispreferred option; 不如 (bùrú) names what's better. The whole pattern is a deliberative comparison.

exercises.prompt: "他寧可辭職，也不妥協." The 寧可…也不 pattern signals that the speaker:
options: Strongly prefers the first option, rejecting the second
exercises.answer: Strongly prefers the first option, rejecting the second
exercises.explanation: 寧可…也不 — "would rather X than Y." The first clause is what the speaker chooses; the second is what they refuse, even at cost.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Rather than complain, it's better to take action."
exercises.answer: 與其 抱怨 不如 行動

exercises.prompt: "他平時話不多，關鍵時刻倒是很果斷." What does 倒是 contribute?
options: It introduces a gentle reversal of expectation — "actually / on the contrary"
exercises.answer: It introduces a gentle reversal of expectation — "actually / on the contrary"
exercises.explanation: 倒是 (dàoshì) is a soft contrastive — softer than 反而, conversational-formal. It signals that despite what one might expect, the opposite is true.

exercises.prompt: "你這麼一說，我 ___ 想起來了." Fill the discourse marker that means "actually / now that you mention it."
exercises.answer: 倒是
exercises.explanation: 倒是 (or just 倒) marks the gentle realization — your remark caused an unexpected memory.

exercises.prompt: Build a long deliberative sentence: "He would rather sacrifice short-term profit than betray the trust of his customers."
exercises.answer: 他 寧可 犧牲 短期 利益 也不 辜負 客戶 的 信任

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads four versions. Pick the one with the cleanest 與其…不如… cadence.
exercises.spokenText: 與其坐而論道，不如起而行之
options: 與其坐而論道，不如起而行之
與其在那裡坐著空談道理，不如起來就趕緊去行動
與其討論，不如行動起來積極地解決問題
與其坐下來談論各種道理，不如行動
exercises.answer: 與其坐而論道，不如起而行之
exercises.explanation: Two 4-character clauses with mirrored grammar (verb 而 verb-object). Classical-flavored balance — the C2 essay closer. The padded distractors lose the rhythm.

exercises.prompt: the choice/preference pattern to its rhetorical use

pairs.right: Recommending the better of two options
Strong preference, refusing the alternative at cost

exercises.prompt: Which captures the difference between 倒是 and 反而 most accurately?
options: 倒是 is sharper than 反而
倒是 is softer / more conversational; 反而 is sharper, often signaling unexpected counter-result
反而 is colloquial and 倒是 is rude
exercises.answer: 倒是 is softer / more conversational; 反而 is sharper, often signaling unexpected counter-result
exercises.explanation: 倒是 is a gentle reversal ("actually / as it happens"); 反而 marks a stronger, often surprising counter-result. C2 readers feel the difference instantly.

exercises.prompt: Complete the proverb-style line: "___ 抱怨 命運 不公 ， ___ 改寫 自己 的 故事." Fill the deliberative pair (2 + 2 characters).
exercises.answer: 與其 不如
exercises.explanation: 與其抱怨命運不公，不如改寫自己的故事 — "rather than complain about an unfair fate, better to rewrite your own story." Classic motivational rhetoric in deliberative cadence.

lessons.title: Dialogue: Editing an op-ed
lessons.description: A journalist defends rhetorical choices to a sharp editor.

exercises.prompt: Op-ed revision with the senior editor

turns.speaker: zhao
turns.text: 稿子我看了，開篇用了排比，氣勢是有的。(gǎo zi wǒ kàn le, kāi piān yòng le pái bǐ, qì shì shì yǒu de.)
turns.spokenText: 稿子我看了，開篇用了排比，氣勢是有的。

turns.speaker: zhao
turns.text: 但第二段「政策如春風，似細雨，若朝陽」——這是哪種修辭？(dàn dì èr duàn zhèng cè rú chūn fēng, sì xì yǔ, ruò zhāo yáng — zhè shì nǎ zhǒng xiū cí?)
turns.spokenText: 但第二段「政策如春風，似細雨，若朝陽」——這是哪種修辭？

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Name the figure used by the writer.
options: 排比 + 比喻 (pái bǐ + bǐ yù – parallelism with simile)
turns.answer: 排比 + 比喻 (pái bǐ + bǐ yù – parallelism with simile)

turns.speaker: zhao
turns.text: 不錯。但第三段那句反問，未免太重，讀者會覺得說教。(bù cuò. dàn dì sān duàn nà jù fǎn wèn, wèi miǎn tài zhòng, dú zhě huì jué de shuō jiào.)
turns.spokenText: 不錯。但第三段那句反問，未免太重，讀者會覺得說教。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Choose the most diplomatic professional reply.
options: 我改成陳述句，留一分餘地。(wǒ gǎi chéng chén shù jù, liú yī fēn yú dì.)
隨便你，反正我懶得改。(suí biàn nǐ, fǎn zhèng wǒ lǎn de gǎi.)
你不懂修辭。(nǐ bù dǒng xiū cí.)
這有什麼好挑的？(zhè yǒu shén me hǎo tiāo de?)
turns.answer: 我改成陳述句，留一分餘地。(wǒ gǎi chéng chén shù jù, liú yī fēn yú dì.)

turns.speaker: zhao
turns.text: 好。結尾「不可不察也」——這「也」是古意還是口語？(hǎo. jié wěi bù kě bù chá yě — zhè yě shì gǔ yì hái shì kǒu yǔ?)
turns.spokenText: 好。結尾「不可不察也」——這「也」是古意還是口語？

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Which register is 「不可不察也」?

turns.speaker: zhao
turns.text: 正是。社論結尾用它，分量自重。(zhèng shì. shè lùn jié wěi yòng tā, fèn liàng zì zhòng.)
turns.spokenText: 正是。社論結尾用它，分量自重。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Fill the connector for "yet/and so" in: 富___不驕 (rich yet not arrogant).

turns.speaker: zhao
turns.text: 「富而不驕」——好句子。明早九點見報。(fù ér bù jiāo — hǎo jù zi. míng zǎo jiǔ diǎn jiàn bào.)
turns.spokenText: 「富而不驕」——好句子。明早九點見報。

topics.title: 成語 and 歇後語 mastery
topics.description: Higher-tier idioms plus the two-part allegorical sayings of everyday speech

lessons.title: Higher-tier 成語
lessons.description: Six idioms that mark you as a serious reader

exercises.prompt: the 成語 to its meaning
Your team raises 1% of what is needed for disaster relief. A reporter writes: "這點捐款無異於___。" Best fit?
exercises.answer: 杯水車薪
exercises.explanation: 杯水車薪 = a cup of water on a burning cartload — the textbook idiom for hopelessly insufficient help.

exercises.prompt: An alumnus donates a building and says "我只是___罷了." What did they say?
exercises.answer: 飲水思源
exercises.explanation: 飲水思源 — "drink water, remember its source." The standard humble phrase for a former student giving back.

exercises.prompt: A junior researcher publishes a quiet paper that quietly changes the field. Years later, a colleague says "她那篇論文真是 ___ — 之前大家幾乎都沒聽過她的名字." Fill the blank.
exercises.answer: 一鳴驚人
acceptableAnswers: 一鳴驚人 (yī míng jīng rén)
exercises.explanation: 一鳴驚人 — "one cry stuns everyone" — fits an unknown who astonishes. Standalone, without a near-synonym crowding it.

exercises.prompt: the higher-tier 成語 to its literal image

pairs.right: Crows and sparrows make no sound
A cup of water for a cartload of burning firewood

exercises.prompt: An editorial about a record-breaking heatwave opens with "今夏的高溫實屬___，氣象臺近百年來從未記錄過同等資料." Best fit?
exercises.answer: 前所未有
exercises.explanation: 前所未有 — "unprecedented" — fits records that break the historical baseline. Standard editorial collocation.

exercises.prompt: A judge enters the courtroom and the gallery instantly falls silent. A reporter writes "全場頓時___." Best fit?
exercises.answer: 鴉雀無聲
exercises.explanation: 鴉雀無聲 — even crows and sparrows are silent — is the textbook idiom for an instantly hushed crowd.

exercises.prompt: An award citation reads: "她獲此殊榮，可謂 ___ — 多年的耕耘終於得到了應有的認可." Pick the idiom that says "the reputation is earned."
exercises.answer: 名副其實
acceptableAnswers: 名副其實 (míng fù qí shí)
exercises.explanation: 名副其實 — name matches reality — the standard endorsement of an earned title or reputation.

exercises.prompt: A tech blog warns: "創業者一夜爆紅的故事 ___，但持續輸出價值才是真正的難題." Pick the idiom signaling "unprecedented and stunning."
exercises.answer: 一鳴驚人
exercises.explanation: 一鳴驚人 here describes the splashy debut. The follow-up clause then deflates it — classic editorial rhythm.

exercises.prompt: Which of these would feel WRONG in an op-ed about fundraising falling short?
options: 募集到的款項不過 杯水車薪
募集到的款項實屬 鴉雀無聲
對受災群眾而言，杯水車薪也聊勝於無
面對龐大的缺口，這點錢無異於杯水車薪
exercises.answer: 募集到的款項實屬 鴉雀無聲
exercises.explanation: 鴉雀無聲 describes a silent crowd, not insufficient funds. A native reader would feel the misfit instantly. Distractor-spotting at C2 means recognizing the image inside each idiom.

lessons.title: 塞翁失馬 and the long forms
lessons.description: Idioms whose punchline is implied

exercises.prompt: "塞翁失馬" is short for "塞翁失馬，焉知非福." The full meaning is:
options: Bad luck now may prove to be good fortune later
A horse lost is a horse gone
The wise farmer never loses anything
exercises.answer: Bad luck now may prove to be good fortune later

exercises.prompt: Your friend missed a flight that later had a maintenance scare. Best response:
options: 看來是塞翁失馬 — talk about a blessing in disguise.
真是杯水車薪 — that hardly helps at all.
果然是名副其實 — the reputation is earned.
確實是鴉雀無聲 — you can hear a pin drop.
exercises.answer: 看來是塞翁失馬 — talk about a blessing in disguise.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Don't worry — this may turn out to be a blessing in disguise."
exercises.answer: 別 擔心 這 或許 是 塞翁失馬

exercises.prompt: the long-form idiom to the punchline that completes it
"百聞不如一見" is best paraphrased as:
options: Hearing a hundred times is not as good as seeing once
It is better to hear than to see
A hundred questions deserve one answer
exercises.answer: Hearing a hundred times is not as good as seeing once
exercises.explanation: The idiom is a stock argument for first-hand experience. Often quoted before someone visits a place they have only read about.

exercises.prompt: An interviewee says "我相信 三人行必有我師." The implied register is:
options: Confucian humility — there is always something to learn from others
A literal claim about three travelers
exercises.answer: Confucian humility — there is always something to learn from others
exercises.explanation: From 論語. Quoted to signal teachability without sounding self-deprecating.

exercises.prompt: After a startup pivot succeeds, the founder writes "當初被裁員，如今想來真是 ___ ， 焉知非福." Fill the missing four characters.
exercises.answer: 塞翁失馬
acceptableAnswers: 塞翁失馬 (sài wēng shī mǎ)
exercises.explanation: 塞翁失馬，焉知非福 — the long form. Setting the punchline behind the comma is a common rhetorical pattern.

exercises.prompt: Which scenario LEAST fits 塞翁失馬?
options: A canceled flight that avoids a maintenance issue
A failed job application that pushes someone into a better field
A chronic illness that forces healthier habits
A long-planned promotion that arrives on schedule
exercises.answer: A long-planned promotion that arrives on schedule
exercises.explanation: 塞翁失馬 requires an initial misfortune that turns out for the best. A smooth, on-time success is just success.

exercises.prompt: Build the long form: "Old man at the frontier loses his horse — how to know it isn't fortune?"
exercises.answer: 塞翁 失馬 焉 知 非 福

exercises.prompt: A professor quotes "學而不思則罔". The point being made is:
options: Learning without reflection leaves you confused / lost
Thinking is more important than learning
Both learning and thinking are useless
exercises.answer: Learning without reflection leaves you confused / lost
exercises.explanation: The full Analects line: 學而不思則罔，思而不學則殆 — both halves needed. 罔 here is closer to "lost / muddled" than "empty."

lessons.title: 歇後語 — set-up and punchline
lessons.description: The two-part sayings every native speaker recognizes

exercises.prompt: the set-up to the punchline
A coworker says "我現在真是泥菩薩過江啊…" They mean:
options: I can't help you — I'm in trouble myself
exercises.answer: I can't help you — I'm in trouble myself
exercises.explanation: The implied 自身難保 — "can't even save myself." A polite way to refuse a favor.

topics.title: Confucian and Daoist concepts
topics.description: 仁、義、道、無為 — the philosophical vocabulary in modern usage

guide.intro: Modern Mandarin is haunted by two-and-a-half-thousand-year-old conversations. Words like 仁 (rén), 义 (yì), 道 (dào), and 无为 (wú wéi) appear in HR slogans, parenting books, and political speeches — usually drained of their original technical force, but never entirely. To read Chinese deeply you have to feel the philosophical residue.

sections.text: Confucian core: 仁 and 義

仁 (rén) is humaneness — the disposition to treat others as fully human. 義 (yì) is righteousness — doing the right thing even at cost. The compound 仁義 is shorthand for moral character. When a CEO is praised as 有仁義 (yǒu rén yì), they are being called principled, not merely successful.

rows.source: 他 是 一 個 仁義 之 人。
rows.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè rényì zhī rén.
rows.translation: He is a man of humaneness and integrity.

rows.source: 見 利 忘 義
rows.translation: See profit and forget righteousness — chase money and ditch principle.
Give up life to grasp righteousness — die for principle.

sections.text: 禮 — propriety, ritual, manners

禮 (lǐ) is the choreography of how relationships should be enacted — bowing depths, gift weights, who eats first. In modern business, 禮 survives as 禮貌 (politeness), 禮物 (gift), 送禮 (gift-giving), and the everyday verb 失禮 (to be rude / lose face by a breach of manners).

rows.source: 禮 多 人 不 怪
rows.translation: Excessive courtesy is never resented.

rows.source: 來 而 不 往 非 禮 也
rows.pinyin: Lái ér bù wǎng fēi lǐ yě
rows.translation: To receive and not give back is not 礼 — i.e. you must reciprocate.

sections.text: Daoist counterweight: 道 and 無為

道 (dào) is the underlying way of things — natural, ungraspable. 無為 (wú wéi) is "non-coercive action" — accomplishing through alignment rather than force. Modern usage has softened both: 道理 (reason, principle), 知道 (literally "know the way" — the everyday "to know"), 無為而治 (governing by stepping back).

rows.translation: Follow its natural course — let things be.
Govern by non-action — manage by enabling, not directing.
The highest good is like water — yielding, low-seeking, ultimately unstoppable.

sections.text: 上善若水 from the 道德經 is engraved on countless tea-shop walls and tech-CEO LinkedIn bios. Recognize it as Daoist signaling — humility-by-quotation.
中庸 — the middle way

中庸 (zhōng yōng), "the doctrine of the mean," prizes balance over extremes. In modern business and family advice, 中庸之道 (zhōng yōng zhī dào) is the polite phrase for "don't overdo it either way." Speakers reaching for it want to sound measured, even-keeled, philosophically grounded.

rows.source: 我 主張 走 中庸 之 道。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ zhǔzhāng zǒu zhōngyōng zhī dào.
rows.translation: I advocate the middle way.

sections.text: Be careful: 中庸 in younger urban use can be subtly negative — "wishy-washy, refuses to take a side." Read the speaker's tone.

lessons.title: 仁 and 義 in modern speech
lessons.description: When someone is praised as 仁義

exercises.prompt: the term to its closest English
"見利忘義" describes someone who:
exercises.answer: Sees profit and abandons principle
exercises.explanation: A standard accusation in business journalism — pursuing money at the cost of ethics.

exercises.prompt: "捨生取___" — fill in the missing concept ("give up life to grasp ___").
exercises.answer: 義
exercises.explanation: 捨生取義 — die for righteousness. Quoted of martyrs and people of principle.

exercises.prompt: the four Confucian virtues to their domain

pairs.right: Doing the right thing at cost

exercises.prompt: When a CEO is publicly described as "有仁義" by a long-time employee, the implication is:
options: Principled — treats people fairly even when costly
exercises.answer: Principled — treats people fairly even when costly
exercises.explanation: 仁義 in modern usage means moral character, not abstract virtue. It is reserved for people who pay personal costs for principle.

exercises.prompt: "禮多人不怪" carries which practical advice?
options: Be polite — even an excess of courtesy is rarely held against you
Skip the formalities to save time
exercises.answer: Be polite — even an excess of courtesy is rarely held against you

exercises.prompt: An accusation in business journalism: a partner who walks away with cash at the first sign of profit is described as "___ 利忘義". Fill in the missing character.
exercises.answer: 見
exercises.explanation: 見利忘義 — see profit and forget righteousness. The 見 (see, encounter) governs 利, with 忘義 the consequence.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence most clearly uses 禮 in its modern "manners / propriety" sense rather than its ritual sense?
options: 國之大事，在祀與戎，禮不可廢。
exercises.answer: 對長輩說話要有禮貌。
exercises.explanation: 禮貌 is the modern compound — "politeness, manners." The other three sentences use 禮 in its classical/ritual sense.

exercises.prompt: Build: "To see profit and forget righteousness — this kind of person cannot be trusted."
exercises.answer: 見 利 忘 義 這 種 人 不 可 信

exercises.prompt: A eulogy says "先生一生 ___ , 受人敬重." The most natural Confucian phrase:
exercises.answer: 仁義為懷
exercises.explanation: 仁義為懷 — "with humaneness and righteousness held in the heart" — the standard eulogy register for a person of principle.

lessons.title: 道 and 無為 — Daoist register
lessons.description: 順其自然, 上善若水, and the language of stepping back

exercises.prompt: "順其自然" is roughly:
exercises.answer: Let nature take its course
exercises.explanation: A Daoist-flavored consolation phrase. Said to friends who can't fix what isn't theirs to fix.

exercises.prompt: A founder posts "上善若水" on their wall. They are signaling:
options: Daoist humility — yielding, patient, ultimately unstoppable
exercises.answer: Daoist humility — yielding, patient, ultimately unstoppable

exercises.prompt: Build: "My management style is one of non-action governance."
exercises.answer: 我 的 管理 風格 是 無 為 而 治

exercises.prompt: the Daoist phrase to the situation it suits

pairs.right: Console a friend — let it be

exercises.prompt: "無為而治" most precisely means:
options: Govern through inaction — laziness as policy
Govern through alignment rather than coercion — minimal intervention
exercises.answer: Govern through alignment rather than coercion — minimal intervention
exercises.explanation: 無為 is non-coercive action, not zero action. Modern usage often softens it further to "hands-off management."

exercises.prompt: Engraved on the wall of a tea shop: "上善若 ___ ." Fill in the missing character.
exercises.answer: 水
exercises.explanation: 上善若水 from 道德經. Water yields, seeks the low, and ultimately wears down stone — the Daoist ideal of soft strength.

exercises.prompt: A friend's plan keeps falling apart. The Daoist-flavored consolation is:
exercises.answer: 順其自然吧
exercises.explanation: 順其自然 acknowledges the situation without blame — the standard Daoist consolation.

exercises.prompt: Modern 知道 ("to know") was historically built from 知 + 道. The classical sense was:
options: To know the Way / understand the underlying order
exercises.answer: To know the Way / understand the underlying order
exercises.explanation: Modern 知道 is now generic "know," but the etymology preserves the Daoist 道 — "grasp the Way."

exercises.prompt: An entrepreneur says her management style is "無為而治." A skeptical employee might mentally translate this as:
options: She lets things drift while sounding philosophical about it
exercises.answer: She lets things drift while sounding philosophical about it
exercises.explanation: 無為而治 has a real meaning, but in modern corporate speech it can also be a self-flattering label for absentee leadership. C2 reading means hearing both registers.

exercises.prompt: Build the philosophical-flavored line: "The highest good is like water; it benefits all and contends with none."
exercises.answer: 上 善 若 水 利 萬 物 而 不 爭

lessons.title: 中庸 and the rhetoric of balance
lessons.description: The middle way — and when it sounds like a dodge

exercises.prompt: A senior advisor says "我們走中庸之道." What does this likely signal in a meeting?
options: We will pick the most extreme option
exercises.answer: We will balance / avoid extremes

exercises.prompt: Among urban younger speakers, "太中庸了" can mean:
options: Wishy-washy / refusing to take a side
exercises.answer: Wishy-washy / refusing to take a side
exercises.explanation: Same word, opposite valence — context and tone decide. Read the room before quoting Confucius.

exercises.prompt: "禮多人不怪" means: even excessive ___ is not resented.
exercises.answer: Politeness

exercises.prompt: the rhetorical move to its phrase

pairs.right: Going too far is as bad as falling short
Just right — neither over nor under

exercises.prompt: "過猶不及" — the classical principle behind 中庸 — claims that:
options: Excess is always better than deficiency
Going too far is as bad as not going far enough
exercises.answer: Going too far is as bad as not going far enough
exercises.explanation: From the Analects. The most common technical formulation of 中庸 — neither extreme is acceptable.

exercises.prompt: An older boss says "凡事 適可而止 ." The advice is closest to:
options: Push as hard as you can
Know when to stop — don't overdo it
exercises.answer: Know when to stop — don't overdo it
exercises.explanation: 適可而止 — "stop where appropriate." Conservative life advice with a Confucian undertow.

exercises.prompt: A wine expert praises a vintage as "___ 到好處, 既不過濃也不過淡." Fill the blank.
exercises.answer: 恰
exercises.explanation: 恰到好處 — exactly right. Note the rhythmic pairing with 不過濃也不過淡 — a parallel construction.

exercises.prompt: A senior advisor closes a meeting with "我們走中庸之道吧." In the same firm, a younger manager later messages a colleague "老闆太中庸了." What is the difference in valence?
options: First is principled balance; second is "wishy-washy / refuses to take a side"
They are simply restating each other
exercises.answer: First is principled balance; second is "wishy-washy / refuses to take a side"
exercises.explanation: The same word can read as moral discipline or as evasion depending on speaker, listener, and tone. C2 means tracking both.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase is LEAST related to the rhetoric of moderation?
exercises.answer: 捨生取義
exercises.explanation: 捨生取義 — die for principle — is the rhetoric of moral extremism, not moderation. The other three all gesture toward balance.

exercises.prompt: Build: "In all things, going too far is as bad as falling short."
exercises.answer: 凡 事 過 猶 不 及

lessons.description: How philosophical phrases land in modern arguments

exercises.prompt: the canonical phrase to its modern use

pairs.right: Said to console — let it be
We're going to split the difference

exercises.prompt: A friend's startup folds. The most fitting consolation:
exercises.answer: 順其自然吧
exercises.explanation: 順其自然 acknowledges the loss while declining to assign blame — the ideal consolation phrase.

exercises.prompt: Build: "He really is a man of integrity."

exercises.prompt: the canonical source to a phrase from it
"三人行，必有我師" comes from which classical source?
exercises.answer: 論語

exercises.prompt: An academic essay quotes "上善若水" in its concluding paragraph. The likely intent is:

To make a literal claim about hydrology
exercises.answer: To frame humility / yielding strength as the essay's stance
exercises.explanation: Closing-paragraph quotations are stance-setting. 上善若水 reaches for Daoist authority on yielding.

exercises.prompt: Which is the philosophical school behind "無為而治"?
exercises.answer: 道家 (Daoist)
exercises.explanation: Non-coercive governance is the Daoist political ideal. Legalists wanted strict laws; Confucians wanted ritual order.

exercises.prompt: Which is the philosophical school behind "克己復禮" (subdue the self and return to ritual)?
exercises.answer: 儒家
exercises.explanation: 克己復禮 is from the Analects — Confucius' definition of 仁. A Confucian fingerprint.

exercises.answer: 義

topics.title: Regional language awareness
topics.description: Mainland Putonghua, Taiwan Guoyu, and the Cantonese world

guide.intro: "Chinese" is several languages and several standardizations of one. C2 means you can hear someone speak for ten seconds and tell whether they grew up in Beijing, Taipei, Guangzhou, or Singapore — and adjust your own usage accordingly. You won't speak every variant. You will learn to recognize and respect them.

sections.text: Putonghua vs Guoyu — same language, different standard

Mainland 普通話 (pǔtōnghuà) and Taiwan 國語 (guóyǔ) are the same language with different standardizations: simplified vs traditional characters, mainland Pinyin vs Taiwanese Zhuyin (注音), distinct vocabulary for many modern objects.
On the mainland 土豆 = potato. In Taiwan 土豆 = peanut. This single word has caused decades of dinner-party confusion.
Tone and accent cues

Mainland Putonghua, especially Beijing-flavored, has heavy 兒化音 (érhuàyīn, the rhotic suffix) — 哪兒、玩兒、有點兒. Taiwan Guoyu generally drops 兒化, prefers softer tones, and sounds the neutral tone less aggressively. Southern mainland speakers (Shanghai, Guangzhou) often blur the n/l distinction or merge zh/z, ch/c, sh/s.

rows.translation: Where are you? — Beijing-flavored.
Where are you? — Taiwan / southern / formal.

sections.text: Cantonese — a separate Chinese language

廣東話 / 粵語 (Cantonese) is mutually unintelligible with Mandarin in speech, though written Standard Chinese is shared. Cantonese has six tones (some count nine), retains classical Chinese consonant clusters lost in Mandarin, and uses distinct vocabulary: 唔 (m̀h, not) for 不, 佢 (kéuih) for 他, 食 (sihk) for 吃.

rows.translation: Have you eaten? — Cantonese, written informally.

rows.source: 你 吃 了 飯 沒有？
rows.pinyin: Nǐ chī le fàn méi yǒu? (Mandarin)
rows.translation: Same question, Mandarin.

sections.text: When you see characters like 嘅、咗、嗮、咩、嘢 in writing — that's written Cantonese (粵文), common on Hong Kong social media but unusual in mainland publications.
Singapore, Malaysia, overseas

Singaporean Mandarin (新加坡華語) is heavily code-mixed with English, Hokkien, and Malay. Vocabulary like 巴剎 (bāshā, market — from Malay pasar) and 德士 (déshì, taxi — from English) is locally standard but invisible on the mainland. Malaysian Chinese communities use similar mixes. Overseas Chinese in the US/Australia often retain pre-1949 vocabulary — 老中 for "older Chinese folks," or older transliterations.
Cross-strait political vocabulary — read the labels

Political register is where word choice tells you the speaker's stance. 大陸 (dàlù, "the mainland") and 內地 (nèidì, "the interior") describe the same territory but signal different framings — 內地 is the term Hong Kong and Macau use within the One-Country framework; Taiwan media usually prefer 中國大陸 or simply 中國. Likewise, 政府 (zhèngfǔ) is neutral "government," while 當局 (dāngjú, "the authorities") is more distanced — used by foreign-press translations and by speakers who want a faintly skeptical tone.

rows: Taiwan media, Hong Kong, overseas Chinese
"The interior" — frames PRC as the inside

sections.text: These choices are not interchangeable. Calling Taiwan's elected government 臺灣當局 ("the Taiwan authorities") rather than 臺灣政府 is itself a political signal — standard in PRC official media. Reading register includes reading these tells.

lessons.title: Mainland vs Taiwan vocab
lessons.description: Same idea, different word

exercises.prompt: the mainland term to its Taiwan counterpart
A Taiwanese friend says "我愛吃土豆." They probably mean:
exercises.answer: Peanuts
exercises.explanation: Mainland 土豆 = potato. In Taiwan, 土豆 = peanut. The same characters; different referent.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is most clearly a mainland register?
exercises.answer: 我去坐地鐵上班。
exercises.explanation: 地鐵 + 坐 is mainland-standard. 捷運 is the Taipei system; 巴士 is Hong Kong / Cantonese for bus.

exercises.prompt: On the mainland, the word for "pineapple" is ___.
exercises.answer: 菠蘿

exercises.prompt: each word to the region where it is the local standard
A Taiwanese tech blogger writes "我電腦裡的軟體好舊了." The mainland speaker would most naturally write:
options: 我電腦裡的軟體好舊了
我電腦裡的硬體好舊了
我電腦裡的影片好舊了
我電腦裡的程式好舊了
exercises.answer: 我電腦裡的軟體好舊了
exercises.explanation: Taiwan 軟體 = mainland 軟體 (software). Both are technically transparent calques but only one is locally standard in each region.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence reads as Taiwan Guoyu rather than mainland Putonghua?
exercises.answer: 我等下要去搭捷運。
exercises.explanation: Taiwan markers cluster: 等下 (in a moment, instead of mainland 待會兒), 搭 (instead of 坐), 捷運 (Taipei subway). The other options are mainland-flavored.

exercises.prompt: Hong Kong newspapers and signage typically write "巴士" rather than mainland "___ ".
exercises.answer: 公交車
exercises.explanation: 巴士 is a transliteration of "bus" via Cantonese; common in HK and overseas Chinese communities. Mainland Putonghua prefers 公交車.

exercises.prompt: A cookbook published in Taipei lists 鳳梨酥 as a specialty. A mainland reader would understand 鳳梨 as:
exercises.answer: Pineapple
exercises.explanation: Taiwan 鳳梨 = mainland 菠蘿. 鳳梨酥 (pineapple cake) is so iconic that the mainland reader recognizes the dish even if the word is regional.

exercises.prompt: Build the Taiwan-flavored sentence: "After work I'll take the metro home."
exercises.answer: 下班 後 我 搭 捷運 回家

lessons.title: Hearing 兒化音
lessons.description: Northern rhotic vs Taiwan / southern smoothness

exercises.prompt: Pick what you hear (Beijing-flavored)
exercises.spokenText: 你在哪兒
exercises.answer: 你在哪兒

exercises.prompt: Pick what you hear (Taiwan / formal)
exercises.spokenText: 你在哪裡
exercises.answer: 你在哪裡

exercises.prompt: Heavy 兒化音 ("那兒", "玩兒") most strongly suggests a speaker from:
exercises.answer: Beijing
exercises.explanation: 兒化音 is a Beijing trademark. Taiwan Guoyu drops it; southern Mandarin uses it sparingly; Singapore essentially never.

exercises.prompt: Beijing-flavored speech — pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 今兒天氣真不錯，咱們出去玩兒玩兒
options: 今兒天氣真不錯，咱們出去玩兒玩兒
今天天氣真不錯，我們出去玩一下
今天天氣挺好的，我們出去走走
今天的天氣很好，我們去公園吧
exercises.answer: 今兒天氣真不錯，咱們出去玩兒玩兒
exercises.explanation: Beijing markers: 今兒 (today, with rhotic), 咱們 (inclusive we, more common in the north), and 玩兒 (rhoticized verb). Compare to flatter southern/Taiwan phrasing.

exercises.prompt: Taiwan-accent speech — pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 我跟你講，這件事情真的有夠麻煩的
options: 我跟你講，這件事情真的有夠麻煩的
我跟你說，這件事真的特別麻煩
我告訴你啊，這事兒真夠麻煩的
跟你說，這事真的好麻煩
exercises.answer: 我跟你講，這件事情真的有夠麻煩的
exercises.explanation: Taiwan markers: 跟你講 (instead of mainland 跟你說), 有夠 (intensifier — distinctively Taiwan), softer sentence-ending 的. The mainland-flavored options use 事兒 with rhotic and 跟你說 / 告訴你.

exercises.prompt: the regional accent feature to the place it points to

pairs.left: Heavy 兒化 (哪兒、玩兒、事兒)

exercises.prompt: A speaker pronounces 知道 as something close to "zī dào" rather than "zhī dào". They are most likely from:
exercises.answer: Shanghai or other southern city
exercises.explanation: Southern mainland speakers commonly merge zh/ch/sh into z/c/s. Northern speakers (Beijing, 東北) preserve the retroflex distinction strongly.

exercises.prompt: Northeast (東北) flavored speech — pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 你這人咋這樣啊，整這些沒用的幹啥
options: 你這人咋這樣啊，整這些沒用的幹啥
你這個人怎麼這樣，做這些沒用的事幹嘛
你怎麼這麼不講理，何必如此
你為什麼這樣做，請你說明原因
exercises.answer: 你這人咋這樣啊，整這些沒用的幹啥
exercises.explanation: 東北 markers: 咋 (=怎麼), 整 (versatile verb meaning "do/handle"), 幹啥 (=做什麼). Strongly colloquial; almost never appears in print outside of dialogue.

exercises.prompt: Which set of features signals a Taiwan speaker rather than a mainland Beijing speaker?
options: 兒化 + 咱們 + 幹啥
無兒化 + 跟你講 + 有夠 + soft sentence-final 的
exercises.answer: 無兒化 + 跟你講 + 有夠 + soft sentence-final 的

exercises.prompt: Singapore Mandarin — pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 我等下去巴剎買點菜，要不要幫你買什麼
options: 我等下去巴剎買點菜，要不要幫你買什麼
我待會兒去菜市場買點兒菜，要不要給你帶點兒什麼
我等會去市場買點東西，需不需要幫你帶些什麼
我馬上去超市買菜，要給你買什麼嗎
exercises.answer: 我等下去巴剎買點菜，要不要幫你買什麼
exercises.explanation: Singapore markers: 巴剎 (Malay-derived word for market), 等下 (Taiwan-style "in a moment"), absence of 兒化, characteristic prosody. Compare to the Beijing-flavored option with 待會兒 / 點兒.

lessons.title: Cantonese on the page
lessons.description: Recognizing 粵文 — written Cantonese

exercises.prompt: You scroll a Hong Kong forum post: "佢話佢唔嚟喇." This is:
exercises.answer: Written Cantonese (粵文)
exercises.explanation: 佢, 唔, 嚟, 喇 are Cantonese-specific characters. The Mandarin equivalent: 他說他不來了.

exercises.prompt: the Cantonese word to its Mandarin equivalent
Spoken Cantonese and spoken Mandarin are:
options: The same with different vocabulary only
exercises.answer: Mutually unintelligible — distinct Chinese languages
exercises.explanation: They share a writing system (mostly) but the spoken forms are linguistically separate.

exercises.prompt: "佢話佢唔嚟喇" — translated into standard Mandarin would be:
exercises.answer: 他說他不來了
exercises.explanation: 佢=他, 話=說, 唔=不, 嚟=來, 喇 ≈ Mandarin sentence-final 了. Letter by letter, the Cantonese line maps onto the Mandarin one.

exercises.prompt: the Cantonese-only character to its function
A Hong Kong news article (not social media) is written in:
options: Standard written Chinese (with traditional characters), spoken as Cantonese
exercises.answer: Standard written Chinese (with traditional characters), spoken as Cantonese
exercises.explanation: HK formal print uses standard written Chinese in traditional characters. 粵文 is reserved for social media, dialogue, and stylistic effect.

exercises.prompt: Cantonese has approximately how many tones?
exercises.answer: 6 (some count 9)
exercises.explanation: Cantonese has six contrastive tones (or nine if you count entering tones separately). Mandarin has only four plus a neutral tone.

exercises.prompt: The Cantonese verb meaning "to eat" — written with a single character — is ___.
exercises.answer: 食
exercises.explanation: 食 is the Cantonese everyday verb where Mandarin uses 吃. The character is shared classical Chinese but only Cantonese keeps it in daily speech.

exercises.prompt: On a Hong Kong forum: "今晚一齊食飯啦." In standard Mandarin this is:
exercises.answer: 今晚一起吃飯吧
exercises.explanation: 一齊=一起, 食=吃, 啦 is a Cantonese sentence-final particle similar to Mandarin 吧.

exercises.prompt: this Cantonese sentence into standard Mandarin: "佢話佢唔食呢啲嘢."
exercises.answer: 他 說 他 不 吃 這 些 東西

lessons.title: Singapore and overseas Chinese
lessons.description: Code-mixed Mandarin and the diaspora

exercises.prompt: "我去巴剎買菜。" Where is the speaker most likely from?
exercises.answer: Singapore / Malaysia
exercises.explanation: 巴剎 (bāshā) is from Malay pasar (market). Locally standard in Singapore/Malaysia, almost never heard on the mainland.

exercises.prompt: "德士" (déshì) is the Singapore word for:
exercises.answer: Taxi
exercises.explanation: From English "taxi." Mainland equivalent: 計程車. Taiwan: 計程車.

exercises.prompt: Mainland Mandarin uses 影片 for video; Taiwan uses ___.
exercises.answer: 影片

exercises.prompt: An article writes "臺灣當局" rather than "臺灣政府". This word choice signals:
options: A PRC-aligned framing — distancing the elected government as "the authorities"
An academic term with no political weight
exercises.answer: A PRC-aligned framing — distancing the elected government as "the authorities"
exercises.explanation: 當局 ("the authorities") refuses the term 政府 ("government"). In cross-strait writing it is a standard PRC-state-media tell. Reading register means catching this.

exercises.prompt: A Hong Kong government press release uses "內地" while a Taiwan newspaper uses "中國大陸" for the same territory. Why?
options: Same referent, different framings — 內地 fits a One-Country frame; 中國大陸 keeps explicit distance
They refer to different time periods
exercises.answer: Same referent, different framings — 內地 fits a One-Country frame; 中國大陸 keeps explicit distance
exercises.explanation: Same place, different rhetorical relationship. 內地 ("the interior") presupposes you're inside the same country; 中國大陸 names it as a separate political entity.

exercises.prompt: the cross-strait term to the framing it carries
An overseas Chinese newspaper writes "老中紛紛搬來這一區." What does "老中" mean here?
exercises.answer: Older generation Chinese folks
exercises.explanation: Diaspora-flavored shorthand for 老一輩中國人. Almost never appears in mainland or Taiwan press; common in US/Australia Chinese papers.

exercises.prompt: Singapore Mandarin is most distinctive for:
options: Code-mixing with English, Hokkien, and Malay
exercises.answer: Code-mixing with English, Hokkien, and Malay
exercises.explanation: Singapore Mandarin sits inside a multilingual ecology; loanwords like 巴剎 (Malay) and 德士 (English) are locally standard, not slang.

exercises.prompt: A Beijing news anchor refers to Taipei's elected government as "臺灣 ___ " rather than "臺灣政府". Fill in the politically loaded term.
exercises.answer: 當局
exercises.explanation: 臺灣當局 is the standard PRC state-media phrasing. The substitution refuses the term 政府 — a small but consistent rhetorical signal.

exercises.prompt: Build the Singapore-flavored sentence: "I'll go to the market in a moment to buy some vegetables."
exercises.answer: 我 等下 去 巴剎 買 點 菜

lessons.description: Recognize 大陸 / 臺灣 / 香港 vocabulary at a noisy dinner.
